task.description: Gate ISS-0056's graph.ex change (commit 0f8bd06, loosened CHK-14 + new CHK-19 fallback-edge check) against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8.
acceptance_criteria: Scope test run and recorded explicitly
Each of INV-1..INV-8 given an explicit APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE verdict
Applicable invariants verified per their How-to-verify procedure with PASS/FAIL recorded

result.summary:
Scope test: reviewed git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (commit 0f8bd06) plus the full branch diff (docs/issues/ISS-0056.yaml, design doc, handoff JSON files, orchestrator.log -- none of those are code). graph.ex's changed functions (check_unpermitted_edge_condition/1, check_human_task_fallback_edge/1, human_task_source?/3, human_task_edge_really_conditioned?/1, human_task_edge_fallback_candidate?/1) operate purely on in-memory %Node{}/%Edge{}/%__MODULE__{} structs already resident in a decoded Graph -- confirmed via grep that graph.ex contains zero 'Repo.' calls, zero 'schema "' declarations, and no migration file is touched anywhere in the branch diff (git diff --stat shows only graph.ex, a design doc, ISS-0056.yaml, and handoff/log JSON). No API route, no response-shaping of a tenant-scoped entity, no lookup-by-ID handler, no secret resolution. Per the role file's scope test this is out of scope for a tenant-data path, but per WF-02 Step 2c and INV-6 the full INV-1..8 sweep is still recorded below rather than short-circuited on the scope test alone, since INV-1 is now a live invariant that must be checked against the diff's content, not just the file's category.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation): APPLIES-test run -- graph.ex declares no Ecto schema, issues no Repo.* calls, and the diff adds/modifies no priv/repo/migrations/*.exs file; the changed code touches zero business tables. Verdict: NOT-APPLICABLE (no tenant-scoped table, schema, or migration touched -- confirmed by grep, not assumed).
INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no API response type touched, S4 not started.
INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Lua/WASM execution path touched, S5 not started.
INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES-test run -- grep -rn "System.get_env" and the hardcoded-secret heuristic grep against lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex show zero hits; the diff introduces no config/env/token handling of any kind. PASS.
INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE -- no lookup-by-ID endpoint touched, S4 not started.
INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping): APPLIES (meta-invariant, always applies) -- this handoff itself is the proof artefact; no new data-access path was introduced by this diff (confirmed above), so there is nothing further to prove. PASS.
INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): APPLIES-test run -- grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/ priv/repo/migrations/ shows zero hits inside graph.ex, and the diff touches no migration file. PASS.
INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES-test run -- grep -rn '^\s*{:ok, .*} = ' lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex shows zero hits; all new logic (check_unpermitted_edge_condition/1, check_human_task_fallback_edge/1, human_task_source?/3, and the two new predicates) is built from Enum.filter/Enum.map/Enum.any? and a defensive case Map.fetch(...) do {:ok,_}->...; :error->false end in human_task_source?/3 that explicitly handles the dangling-edge miss case rather than pattern-matching only {:ok, _} -- consistent with the existing exclusive_gateway_source?/3 convention. No bare match that can raise on realistic (malformed/dangling-edge) input. PASS.

All applicable invariants PASS; INV-2/3/5 correctly NOT-APPLICABLE (pre-S4/S5); INV-1 explicitly tested against the diff's content (not defaulted) and found NOT-APPLICABLE because no tenant-scoped table/schema/migration is touched -- consistent with security-reviewer.md's guidance that INV-1 applies to diffs touching tenant-scoped tables/schemas/migrations, which this diff does not.
